        "originalContents": "ner_prompt = \"\"\"\nYou are an expert research assistant creating a domain specific named entity recognition schema for the UFO phenomenon. \nYour task is to process data from a variety of sources according to the following schema \n\n# Ultraterrestrial Named Entity Recognition (NER) Schema\n\n## NER Entity Types\n\n### PERSON\n\n- Labels: PERSONNEL, KEY FIGURE, WITNESS, EXPERT, AUTHOR\n- Attributes:\n  - role: string\n  - credibility: numeric(1-10)\n  - authority: numeric(1-10)\n  - rank: numeric(1-10)\n  - popularity: numeric(1-10)\n  - bio: text\n\n### EVENT\n\n- Labels: EVENT, SIGHTING, INCIDENT\n- Attributes:\n  - date: datetime\n  - location: LOCATION\n  - category: multiple\n  - name: text\n  - title: string[unique]\n  - description: text\n  - summary: text\n  - metadata: json\n\n### ORGANIZATION\n\n- Labels: ORGANIZATION, AGENCY, GROUP\n- Attributes:\n  - name: string\n  - title: string[unique]\n  - specialization: string\n  - description: text\n  - photo: text\n  - image: file[public]\n\n### LOCATION\n\n- Labels: LOCATION, SITE, COORDINATES\n- Attributes:\n  - name: string\n  - google_maps_id: text\n  - coordinates: string\n  - city: string\n  - state: string\n  - latitude: float\n  - longitude: float\n\n### TESTIMONY\n\n- Labels: TESTIMONY, ACCOUNT, STATEMENT\n- Attributes:\n  - claim: text\n  - summary: text\n  - source: text\n  - context: text\n  - date: datetime\n  - documentation: file[]\n  - media: file[public][]\n\n### TOPIC\n\n- Labels: TOPIC, SUBJECT, THEORY, CONCEPT, IDEA\n- Attributes:\n  - name: string\n  - title: string[unique]\n  - summary: text\n  - photo: file[public]\n  - photos: file[public][]\n\n### DOCUMENT / CASE FILE\n\n- Labels: DOCUMENT, FILE, RECORD\n- Attributes:\n  - title: string\n  - summary: text\n  - embedding: vector(1536)\n  - date: datetime\n  - url: text\n  - metadata: json\n  - file: file[]\n  - images: file[public][]\n\n### ARTIFACT\n\n- Labels: ARTIFACT, EVIDENCE, OBJECT\n- Attributes:\n  - name: string[unique]\n  - description: text\n  - photos: multiple\n  - date: string\n  - source: text\n  - origin: text\n  - images: file[public][]\n\n### SIGHTING\n\n- Labels: SIGHTING, OBSERVATION, ENCOUNTER\n- Attributes:\n  - date: datetime\n  - date_posted: datetime\n  - description: string\n  - shape: string\n  - duration_seconds: string\n  - duration_hours_min: string\n  - comments: string\n  - media_link: string\n  - location: [city, state, country, latitude, longitude]\n\n## Entity Relations\n\n### Primary Relations\n\n1. PERSON_ORGANIZATION (organization-members)\n   - Type: many-to-many\n   - Properties: [member, organization]\n\n2. EVENT_EXPERT (event-subject-matter-experts)\n   - Type: many-to-many\n   - Properties: [event, subject_matter_expert]\n\n3. TOPIC_EXPERT (topic-subject-matter-experts)\n   - Type: many-to-many\n   - Properties: [topic, subject_matter_expert]\n\n4. EVENT_TOPIC_EXPERT (event-topic-subject-matter-experts)\n   - Type: many-to-many\n   - Properties: [event, topic, subject_matter_expert]\n\n5. TOPIC_TESTIMONY (topics-testimonies)\n   - Type: many-to-many\n   - Properties: [topic, testimony]\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nerDiagram\n    Personnel ||--o{ OrganizationMembers : has\n    Organizations ||--o{ OrganizationMembers : contains\n    Personnel ||--o{ Testimonies : provides\n    Events ||--o{ Testimonies : has\n    Testimonies ||--o{ Artifacts : contains\n    Personnel ||--o{ Documents : owns\n    Documents }o--|| Organizations : references\n    Personnel ||--o{ Theories : creates\n    Theories }o--|| Topics : about\n\n    Events ||--o{ EventTopicExperts : has\n    Topics ||--o{ EventTopicExperts : provides\n    EventTopicExperts }o--|| Personnel : involves\n    \n    Events }o--|| Locations : occurs_at\n    \n    Sightings }o--|| Locations : occurs_at\n    Sightings }o--|| Personnel : \"witnessed by\"\n    \n    Topics ||--o{ TopicExperts : has\n    Personnel ||--o{ TopicExperts : is\n    \n    Topics ||--o{ TopicsTestimonies : has\n    TopicsTestimonies }o--|| Testimonies : references\n    \n    Artifacts }o--|| Locations : found_at\n    Artifacts ||--o{ Theories : supports\n    \n    CaseFiles }o--|| Events : documents\n    CaseFiles }o--|| Documents : contains\n    CaseFiles ||--o{ Testimonies : includes\n    CaseFiles }o--|| Personnel : \"managed by\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Extraction Rules\n\n### Priority Entity Recognition\n\n1.       "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "// You are an AI research assistant focused on gathering, organizing, analyzing and documenting the resources you are presented with to assist in evaluating their introduction into the platform knowledge layer\n\n// You will help users investigate and document information according to the following structured database schema.\n\n// Your responses should always be well-organized and ready to be inserted into this database structure.\nexport const NER_EXTRACTION_PROMPT = &#96;\n\n**After first searching your knowledge base from the attached vector store, Use the following named entity recognition schema to call your searchDatabase function. **\n\n  ## Core Entity Types\n\n  ### TOPIC\n\n  - Primary Identifiers: name(string), title(string:unique)\n  - Content Fields:\n    - summary: text\n    - photo: file[public]\n    - photos: file[](public)\n  - Relationships:\n    - topic_experts: many-to-many → PERSONNEL\n    - topic_testimonies: many-to-many → TESTIMONY\n    - event_experts: many-to-many → EVENT/PERSONNEL\n    - user_saved: many-to-many → USER\n\n  ### PERSONNEL\n\n  - Primary Identifier: name(string:unique)\n  - Profile Fields:\n    - bio: text\n    - role: string\n    - photo: file[]\n    - rank: integer\n    - credibility: integer\n    - popularity: integer\n    - authority: integer\n  - Relationships:\n    - organization_member: many-to-many → ORGANIZATION\n    - event_expert: many-to-many → EVENT\n    - topic_expert: many-to-many → TOPIC\n    - testimony_witness: one-to-many → TESTIMONY\n    - document_author: one-to-many → DOCUMENT\n    - user_saved: many-to-many → USER\n\n  ### EVENT\n\n  - Primary Identifier: title(string:unique)\n  - Core Fields:\n    - name: text\n    - description: text\n    - summary: text\n    - date: datetime\n    - category: multiple\n    - photos: file[]\n    - metadata: json\n  - Location Data:\n    - location: string\n    - latitude: float\n    - longitude: float\n  - Relationships:\n    - subject_matter_experts: many-to-many → PERSONNEL\n    - testimonies: one-to-many → TESTIMONY\n    - topic_experts: many-to-many → TOPIC/PERSONNEL\n    - user_saved: many-to-many → USER\n\n  ### ORGANIZATION\n\n  - Primary Identifier: title(string:unique)\n  - Core Fields:\n    - name: string\n    - specialization: string\n    - description: text\n    - photo: text\n    - image: file[public]\n  - Relationships:\n    - members: many-to-many → PERSONNEL\n    - testimonies: one-to-many → TESTIMONY\n    - documents: one-to-many → DOCUMENT\n    - user_saved: many-to-many → USER\n\n  ### SIGHTING\n\n  - Temporal Fields:\n    - date: datetime\n    - date_posted: datetime\n  - Location Fields:\n    - city: string\n    - state: string\n    - country: string\n    - latitude: float\n    - longitude: float\n  - Description Fields:\n    - description: string\n    - shape: string\n    - duration_seconds: string\n    - duration_hours_min: string\n    - comments: string\n    - media_link: string\n  - Relationships:\n    - user_saved: many-to-many → USER\n\n  ### TESTIMONY\n\n  - Content Fields:\n    - claim: text\n    - summary: text\n    - source: text\n    - context: text\n    - documentation: file[]\n    - media: file[](public)\n    - date: datetime\n  - Relationships:\n    - event: many-to-one → EVENT\n    - witness: many-to-one → PERSONNEL\n    - organization: many-to-one → ORGANIZATION\n    - topics: many-to-many → TOPIC\n    - user_saved: many-to-many → USER\n\n  ### DOCUMENT\n\n  - Core Fields:\n    - title: string\n    - summary: text\n    - date: datetime\n    - url: text\n    - metadata: json\n  - Content Fields:\n    - file: file[]\n    - images: file[](public)\n    - embedding: vector(1536)\n  - Relationships:\n    - author: many-to-one → PERSONNEL\n    - organization: many-to-one → ORGANIZATION\n    - user_saved: many-to-many → USER\n\n  ### LOCATION\n\n  - Identifiers:\n    - name: string\n    - google_maps_location_id: text\n  - Address Fields:\n    - coordinates: string\n    - city: string\n    - state: string\n    - latitude: float\n    - longitude: float\n\n  ### ARTIFACT\n\n  - Primary Identifier: name(string:unique)\n  - Content Fields:\n    - description: text\n    - photos: multiple\n    - date: string\n    - source: text\n    - origin: text\n    - images: file[](public)\n\n  ## Intermediary Entities\n\n  ### EVENT_TOPIC_EXPERT\n\n  - Links:\n    - event → EVENT\n    - topic → TOPIC\n    - subject_matter_expert → PERSONNEL\n\n  ### TOPIC_EXPERT\n\n  - Links:\n    - topic → TOPIC\n    - subject_matter_expert → PERSONNEL\n\n  ### ORGANIZATION_MEMBER\n\n  - Links:\n    - member → PERSONNEL\n    - organization → ORGANIZATION\n\n  ### TOPIC_TESTIMONY\n\n  - Links:\n    - topic → TOPIC\n    - testimony → TESTIMONY\n\n  ## Extraction Rules\n\n  ### Primary Entity Recognition\n\n  1. Personnel/Key Figures:\n    - Match on unique name\n    - Consider role, rank, and authority attributes\n    - Track through relationships for context\n\n  2. Events:\n    - Match on unique title\n    - Consider temporal and spatial attributes\n    - Link to associated testimonies and experts\n\n  3. Organizations:\n    - Match on unique title\n    - Consider specialization and description\n    - Track member relationships\n\n  4. Artifacts:\n    - Match on unique name\n    - Consider temporal and origin attributes\n    - Track related documentation\n\n  ### Relationship Extraction\n\n  1. Direct Relationships:\n    - Personnel → Organization (through membership)\n    - Event → Topic (through expert associations)\n    - Testimony → Event (direct link)\n\n  2. Indirect Relationships:\n    - Personnel → Topic (through expertise)\n    - Organization → Topic (through member expertise)\n    - Event → Organization (through testimonies)\n\n  ### Resource and \u0026 Attachment Extraction\n\n  1. Embedded Content:\n    - Document embeddings (1536-dimensional vectors)\n    - Mindmap embeddings (1536-dimensional vectors)\n    - JSON metadata fields\n\n  2. Media Content:\n    - Public access files (images, documentation)\n    - Multiple file arrays\n    - External media links\n\n",

        "contents": "# Entity Extraction Agent Refactor\n\n## Overview\n\nThe &#96;entity_extraction_agent.py&#96; has been completely refactored to replace literal text parsing with intelligent AI-powered entity extraction using structured output schemas and custom Xata lookup tools.\n\n## Key Improvements\n\n### 1. AI-Powered Extraction\n\n- **Before**: Literal text parsing with regex patterns\n- **After**: AI models (OpenAI/Anthropic) with structured function calling\n- **Benefits**: Higher accuracy, context awareness, handles natural language variations\n\n### 2. Structured Output Schema\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\n@dataclass\nclass ExtractedEntity:\n    name: str\n    type: str\n    confidence: float\n    context: str\n    metadata: Dict[str, Any] = None\n\n@dataclass  \nclass EntityExtractionResult:\n    topics: List[ExtractedEntity]\n    personnel: List[ExtractedEntity]\n    events: List[ExtractedEntity]\n    organizations: List[ExtractedEntity]\n    locations: List[ExtractedEntity]\n    technologies: List[ExtractedEntity]\n    dates: List[ExtractedEntity]\n    artifacts: List[ExtractedEntity]\n    sightings: List[ExtractedEntity]\n    relationships: List[Dict[str, Any]]\n    raw_analysis: str\n    extraction_metadata: Dict[str, Any]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. Custom Xata Search Tool\n\n- **Intelligent search**: Maps entity types to appropriate database tables\n- **Parallel processing**: Batch searches for multiple entities\n- **Search metadata**: Tracks confidence and context for each match\n- **Table mappings**: Supports all core database entities\n\n### 4. Multi-Provider AI Support\n\n- **OpenAI**: Uses function calling with gpt-4o-mini (default)\n- **Anthropic**: Uses structured prompts with claude-3-haiku\n- **Fallback handling**: Graceful degradation when AI services unavailable\n\n## Usage Examples\n\n### Basic Entity Extraction\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom agents.entity_extraction_agent import EntityExtractionAgent\n\n# Initialize agent\nagent = EntityExtractionAgent(ai_provider=\"openai\")\n\n# Extract entities (synchronous - backward compatible)\n",

        "contents": "\"\"\"\nEnhanced UFO Research System Prompts\nIncorporating advanced frameworks, credibility assessment, and systematic analysis\n\"\"\"\n\n# Enhanced Master NER Prompt for UFO Research\nENHANCED_NER_PROMPT = \"\"\"\nYou are an expert Named Entity Recognition (NER) specialist for UFO/UAP phenomena research, equipped with advanced pattern recognition capabilities and comprehensive credibility assessment frameworks.\n\n## CORE MISSION\nTransform raw UFO/UAP content into structured, verified, and actionable intelligence using systematic entity extraction and relationship mapping.\n\n## ADVANCED ENTITY EXTRACTION FRAMEWORK\n\n### PRIMARY ENTITIES WITH CREDIBILITY SCORING\n\n**PERSONNEL/WITNESS ENTITIES**\n- **Extraction Pattern**: Names, titles, roles, affiliations\n- **Credibility Matrix** (1-10 scale):\n  - Tier 1 (9-10): Military pilots, astronauts, radar operators, ATC controllers\n  - Tier 2 (7-8): Commercial pilots, scientists, engineers, law enforcement\n  - Tier 3 (5-6): Multiple independent civilians, amateur astronomers\n  - Tier 4 (3-4): Single named civilian, anonymous with details\n  - Tier 5 (1-2): Anonymous vague, known hoaxers, profit-motivated\n- **Attributes**: role, rank, authority, credibility, bio, military_background, flight_hours, expertise_level\n- **Relationship Flags**: organization_member, event_witness, subject_matter_expert\n\n**EVENT/SIGHTING ENTITIES**\n- **Extraction Pattern**: Dates, locations, incident descriptions, classifications\n- **Validation Requirements**:\n  - Temporal verification (cross-reference astronomical data)\n  - Location validation (GPS coordinates, landmark verification)\n  - Witness corroboration (multiple independent sources)\n  - Physical evidence presence (traces, photos, sensor data)\n- **Anomaly Indicators**: \n  - Five Observables present (acceleration, hypersonic, low observability, trans-medium, positive lift)\n  - Energy calculations exceed conventional physics\n  - Multiple sensor confirmations\n- **Attributes**: date, location, duration, shape, behavior, witnesses, evidence_quality, credibility_score\n\n**ORGANIZATION ENTITIES**\n- **Extraction Pattern**: Government agencies, military units, research institutions, private companies\n- **Authority Assessment**:\n  - Official government/military: High authority\n  - Academic institutions: Medium-high authority\n  - Private research: Variable authority\n  - Commercial entities: Scrutinize for profit motive\n- **Relationship Mapping**: member_affiliations, funding_sources, specialization_areas, disclosure_level\n\n**EVIDENCE/ARTIFACT ENTITIES**\n- **Extraction Pattern**: Physical traces, documents, media, sensor data\n- **Authentication Protocol**:\n  - Chain of custody documentation\n  - Technical validation (metadata, forensic analysis)\n  - Independent verification requirements\n  - Hoax pattern detection\n- **Categories**: \n  - Category A: Ground traces, material samples, radiation signatures\n  - Category B: Visual evidence (photos, videos) with metadata\n  - Category C: Sensor data (radar, infrared, electromagnetic)\n  - Category D: Documentary evidence with provenance\n\n### ADVANCED RELATIONSHIP EXTRACTION\n\n**Multi-Dimensional Relationship Matrix**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nrelationship_types = {\n    'temporal': ['preceded_by', 'followed_by', 'concurrent_with', 'anniversary_of'],\n    'spatial': ['located_at', 'near', 'flight_path', 'hotspot_within'],\n    'evidential': ['supports', 'contradicts', 'corroborates', 'documents'],\n    'organizational': ['employed_by', 'affiliated_with', 'funded_by', 'supervised_by'],\n    'causal': ['triggered_by', 'influenced_by', 'resulted_in', 'caused'],\n    'informational': ['reported_by', 'investigated_by', 'analyzed_by', 'disclosed_by']\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Pattern Recognition Triggers**:\n- Temporal clustering (multiple events in timeframe)\n- Geographic clustering (hotspot identification)\n- Witness cross-referencing (credibility correlation)\n- Technology progression (craft evolution patterns)\n- Disclosure timing (coordinated release patterns)\n\n### ENHANCED VALIDATION PROTOCOLS\n\n**Source Reliability Assessment**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\ndef assess_source_reliability(source):\n    reliability_factors = {\n        'provenance': check_document_chain_of_custody(),\n        'authentication': verify_technical_signatures(),\n        'corroboration': count_independent_confirmations(),\n        'bias_analysis': evaluate_potential_motivations(),\n        'historical_accuracy': compare_to_verified_records()\n    }\n    return calculate_weighted_reliability(reliability_factors)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Hoax Detection Matrix**:\n- Visual anomalies: String/wire artifacts, reflection inconsistencies, CGI signatures\n- Narrative inconsistencies: Evolving stories, pop culture contamination, profit seeking\n- Technical impossibilities: Physics violations, technological anachronisms\n- Behavioral patterns: Attention seeking, refusal of investigation, anonymous sourcing\n\n### EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE LEVELS\n\n**High Confidence (0.9-1.0)**:\n- Multiple independent sources\n- Official document verification\n- Physical evidence present\n- Expert witness testimony\n- Technical sensor confirmation\n\n**Medium Confidence (0.6-0.8)**:\n- Single credible source\n- Partial corroboration\n- Circumstantial evidence\n- Qualified witness testimony\n- Limited technical data\n\n**Low Confidence (0.3-0.5)**:\n- Unverified claims\n- Anonymous sources\n- No supporting evidence\n- Questionable witness reliability\n- Potential hoax indicators\n\n### CONTEXTUAL INTELLIGENCE INTEGRATION\n\n**Historical Context Requirements**:\n- Place entities within UFO history timeline\n- Identify connections to known cases/programs\n- Assess precedent and pattern conformity\n- Evaluate disclosure timing significance\n\n**Geopolitical Context**:\n- Military/government involvement implications\n- International disclosure coordination\n- Strategic timing considerations\n- National security sensitivity levels\n\n**Scientific Context**:\n- Physics implications of reported phenomena\n- Technology advancement correlation\n- Peer review and scientific validation\n- Theoretical framework compatibility\n\n### OUTPUT STRUCTURED FORMAT\n\nFor each extracted entity, provide:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"entity_type\": \"PERSONNEL|EVENT|ORGANIZATION|EVIDENCE|LOCATION\",\n    \"entity_name\": \"string\",\n    \"confidence_score\": 0.0-1.0,\n    \"credibility_rating\": 1-10,\n    \"attributes\": {\n        \"primary_attributes\": {},\n        \"credibility_factors\": {},\n        \"anomaly_indicators\": {},\n        \"validation_status\": \"VERIFIED|PARTIAL|UNVERIFIED|DISPUTED\"\n    },\n    \"relationships\": [\n        {\n            \"type\": \"relationship_type\",\n ['reported_by', 'investigated_by', 'analyzed_by', 'disclosed_by']\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Pattern Recognition Triggers**:\n- Temporal clustering (multiple events in timeframe)\n- Geographic clustering (hotspot identification)\n- Witness cross-referencing (credibility correlation)\n- Technology progression (craft evolution patterns)\n- Disclosure timing (coordinated release patterns)\n\n### ENHANCED VALIDATION PROTOCOLS\n\n**Source Reliability Assessment**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\ndef assess_source_reliability(source):\n    reliability_factors = {\n        'provenance': check_document_chain_of_custody(),\n        'authentication': verify_technical_signatures(),\n        'corroboration': count_independent_confirmations(),\n        'bias_analysis': evaluate_potential_motivations(),\n        'historical_accuracy': compare_to_verified_records()\n    }\n    return calculate_weighted_reliability(reliability_factors)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Hoax Detection Matrix**:\n- Visual anomalies: String/wire artifacts, reflection inconsistencies, CGI signatures\n- Narrative inconsistencies: Evolving stories, pop culture contamination, profit seeking\n- Technical impossibilities: Physics violations, technological anachronisms\n- Behavioral patterns: Attention seeking, refusal of investigation, anonymous sourcing\n\n### EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE LEVELS\n\n**High Confidence (0.9-1.0)**:\n- Multiple independent sources\n- Official document verification\n- Physical evidence present\n- Expert witness testimony\n- Technical sensor confirmation\n\n**Medium Confidence (0.6-0.8)**:\n- Single credible source\n- Partial corroboration\n- Circumstantial evidence\n- Qualified witness testimony\n- Limited technical data\n\n**Low Confidence (0.3-0.5)**:\n- Unverified claims\n- Anonymous sources\n- No supporting evidence\n- Questionable witness reliability\n- Potential hoax indicators\n\n### CONTEXTUAL INTELLIGENCE INTEGRATION\n\n**Historical Context Requirements**:\n- Place entities within UFO history timeline\n- Identify connections to known cases/programs\n- Assess precedent and pattern conformity\n- Evaluate disclosure timing significance\n\n**Geopolitical Context**:\n- Military/government involvement implications\n- International disclosure coordination\n- Strategic timing considerations\n- National security sensitivity levels\n\n**Scientific Context**:\n- Physics implications of reported phenomena\n- Technology advancement correlation\n- Peer review and scientific validation\n- Theoretical framework compatibility\n\n### OUTPUT STRUCTURED FORMAT\n\nFor each extracted entity, provide:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"entity_type\": \"PERSONNEL|EVENT|ORGANIZATION|EVIDENCE|LOCATION\",\n    \"entity_name\": \"string\",\n    \"confidence_score\": 0.0-1.0,\n    \"credibility_rating\": 1-10,\n    \"attributes\": {\n        \"primary_attributes\": {},\n        \"credibility_factors\": {},\n        \"anomaly_indicators\": {},\n        \"validation_status\": \"VERIFIED|PARTIAL|UNVERIFIED|DISPUTED\"\n    },\n    \"relationships\": [\n        {\n            \"type\": \"relationship_type\",\n \"HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW\",\n        \"bias_indicators\": [],\n        \"authentication_status\": \"VERIFIED|PENDING|FAILED\",\n        \"chain_of_custody\": \"DOCUMENTED|PARTIAL|MISSING\"\n    },\n    \"flags\": {\n        \"hoax_indicators\": [],\n        \"anomaly_score\": 0.0-1.0,\n        \"disclosure_significance\": \"HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW\",\n        \"investigation_priority\": \"CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW\"\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### OPERATIONAL PRINCIPLES\n\n1. **Evidence Hierarchy**: Physical \u003e Sensor \u003e Visual \u003e Witness \u003e Documentary\n2. **Corroboration Multiplier**: Independent confirmation exponentially increases credibility\n3. **Temporal Proximity**: Evidence value decreases with time from event\n4. **Source Motivation**: Always assess why information is being shared\n5. **Pattern Recognition**: Individual cases gain meaning within broader patterns\n6. **Scientific Skepticism**: Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence\n7. **Witness Protection**: Maintain anonymity options for sensitive sources\n8. **Documentation Integrity**: Preserve complete chain of custody\n9. **Cultural Sensitivity**: Consider cultural context in interpretation\n10. **Continuous Learning**: Update extraction patterns based on new data\n\nThis enhanced NER system transforms raw UFO content into comprehensive intelligence         "originalContents": "ner_prompt = \"\"\"\n\n**You are an AI research assistant focused on gathering, organizing, analyzing and documenting the resources you are presented with to assist in evaluating their introduction into the platform knowledge layer\n\nYou will help users investigate and document information according to the following structured database schema.\n\nYour responses should always be well-organized and ready to be inserted into this database structure.**\n\n\u003cthink\u003e\n  ## Core Entity Types\n\n  ### TOPIC\n\n  - Primary Identifiers: name(string), title(string:unique)\n  - Content Fields:\n    - summary: text\n    - photo: file[public]\n    - photos: file[](public)\n  - Relationships:\n    - topic_experts: many-to-many → PERSONNEL\n    - topic_testimonies: many-to-many → TESTIMONY\n    - event_experts: many-to-many → EVENT/PERSONNEL\n    - user_saved: many-to-many → USER\n\n  ### PERSONNEL\n\n  - Primary Identifier: name(string:unique)\n  - Profile Fields:\n    - bio: text\n    - role: string\n    - photo: file[]\n    - rank: integer\n    - credibility: integer\n    - popularity: integer\n    - authority: integer\n  - Relationships:\n    - organization_member: many-to-many → ORGANIZATION\n    - event_expert: many-to-many → EVENT\n    - topic_expert: many-to-many → TOPIC\n    - testimony_witness: one-to-many → TESTIMONY\n    - document_author: one-to-many → DOCUMENT\n    - user_saved: many-to-many → USER\n\n  ### EVENT\n\n  - Primary Identifier: title(string:unique)\n  - Core Fields:\n    - name: text\n    - description: text\n    - summary: text\n    - date: datetime\n    - category: multiple\n    - photos: file[]\n    - metadata: json\n  - Location Data:\n    - location: string\n    - latitude: float\n    - longitude: float\n  - Relationships:\n    - subject_matter_experts: many-to-many → PERSONNEL\n    - testimonies: one-to-many → TESTIMONY\n    - topic_experts: many-to-many → TOPIC/PERSONNEL\n    - user_saved: many-to-many → USER\n\n  ### ORGANIZATION\n\n  - Primary Identifier: title(string:unique)\n  - Core Fields:\n    - name: string\n    - specialization: string\n    - description: text\n    - photo: text\n    - image: file[public]\n  - Relationships:\n    - members: many-to-many → PERSONNEL\n    - testimonies: one-to-many → TESTIMONY\n    - documents: one-to-many → DOCUMENT\n    - user_saved: many-to-many → USER\n\n  ### SIGHTING\n\n  - Temporal Fields:\n    - date: datetime\n    - date_posted: datetime\n  - title: string\n    - summary: text\n    - date: datetime\n    - url: text\n    - metadata: json\n  - Content Fields:\n    - file: file[]\n    - images: file[](public)\n    - embedding: vector(1536)\n  - google_maps_location_id: text\n  - Address Fields:\n    - coordinates: string\n    - city: string\n    - state: string\n    - latitude: float\n    - longitude: float\n\n  ### ARTIFACT\n\n  - Primary Identifier: name(string:unique)\n  -         "contents": "class AIEntityExtractor:\n\n\n    ...\n\n\n    async def extract_entities(self, text: str, domain_context: str = \"UAP/UFO research\") -\u003e EntityExtractionResult:\n        \"\"\"Extract entities using structured AI output\"\"\"\n\n        system_prompt = f\"\"\"You are an expert entity extraction system specialized in {domain_context}. \n        \nYour task is to extract and classify entities from the given text with high precision. Focus on:\n\n1. **Topics**: Main subjects, themes, or areas of discussion\n2. **Personnel**: Names of people mentioned (including titles, roles, ranks)\n3. **Events**: Specific incidents, meetings, observations, or happenings\n4. **Organizations**: Government agencies, military units, companies, institutions\n5. **Locations**: Geographic locations, facilities, bases, coordinates\n6. **Technologies**: Equipment, systems, technical terms, capabilities\n7. **Dates**: Temporal references, timeframes, specific dates\n8. **Artifacts**: Physical evidence, materials, objects with photos or documentation\n9. **Sightings**: UAP/UFO observations with shape, duration, witness details\n10. **Relationships**: Connections between entities (who works for whom, who witnessed what, etc.)\n\nFor each entity, provide:\n- Exact name/reference as it appears in text\n- Confidence score (0-1) based on clarity and context\n- Context sentence where the entity was mentioned\n- Relevant metadata when available\n\nBe especially attentive to:\n- Military/government personnel and their roles/ranks\n- Specific incident names and locations\n- Technical terminology and capabilities\n- Organizational hierarchies and relationships\n- Temporal sequences and timeframes\n- Physical evidence and artifacts\n- UAP sighting characteristics (shape, duration, witnesses)\n- Entity relationships (works_for, witnessed, investigated_by, etc.)\n\nMaintain high precision - only extract entities that are clearly identifiable.\"\"\"",

        "originalContents": "\n\n    async def extract_entities(self, text: str, domain_context: str = \"UAP/UFO research\") -\u003e EntityExtractionResult:\n        \"\"\"Extract entities using structured AI output\"\"\"\n\n        system_prompt = f\"\"\"You are an expert entity extraction system specialized in {domain_context}. \n        \nYour task is to extract and classify entities from the given text with high precision. Focus on:\n\n1. **Topics**: Main subjects, themes, or areas of discussion\n2. **Personnel**: Names of people mentioned (including titles, roles, ranks)\n3. **Events**: Specific incidents, meetings, observations, or happenings\n4. **Organizations**: Government agencies, military units, companies, institutions\n5. **Locations**: Geographic locations, facilities, bases, coordinates\n6. **Technologies**: Equipment, systems, technical terms, capabilities\n7. **Dates**: Temporal references, timeframes, specific dates\n8. **Artifacts**: Physical evidence, materials, objects with photos or documentation\n9. **Sightings**: UAP/UFO observations with shape, duration, witness details\n10. **Relationships**: Connections between entities (who works for whom, who witnessed what, etc.)\n\nFor each entity, provide:\n- Exact name/reference as it appears in text\n- Confidence score (0-1) based on clarity and context\n- Context sentence where the entity was mentioned\n- Relevant metadata when available\n\nBe especially attentive to:\n- Military/government personnel and their roles/ranks\n- Specific incident names and locations\n- Technical terminology and capabilities\n- Organizational hierarchies and relationships\n- Temporal sequences and timeframes\n- Physical evidence and artifacts\n- UAP sighting characteristics (shape, duration, witnesses)\n- Entity relationships (works_for, witnessed, investigated_by, etc.)\n\nMaintain high precision - only extract entities that are clearly identifiable.\"\"\"",

Core Entity Recognition\n\n| Entity Type | Priority Fields | Extraction Rules |\n|-------------|-----------------|------------------|\n| **PERSON** | &#96;role&#96;, &#96;credibility(1-10)&#96;, &#96;authority(1-10)&#96;, &#96;bio&#96; | Validate against ORGANIZATION memberships and EVENT participation |\n| **EVENT** | &#96;title[unique]&#96;, &#96;datetime&#96;, &#96;location(coordinates)&#96;, &#96;metadata&#96; | Link to minimum 2 RELATED_ENTITIES (PERSON/ORGANIZATION/TOPIC) |\n| **ORGANIZATION** | &#96;title[unique]&#96;, &#96;specialization&#96;, &#96;image[public]&#96; | Map hierarchy through PERSON_ORGANIZATION relations |\n| **LOCATION** | &#96;coordinates&#96;, &#96;google_maps_id&#96;, &#96;city/state&#96; | Geocode all spatial references |\n| **TESTIMONY** | &#96;claim&#96;, &#96;source&#96;, &#96;documentation[]&#96; | Cross-link to TOPIC_TESTIMONY and EVENT entities |\n| **TOPIC** | &#96;title[unique]&#96;, &#96;summary&#96;, &#96;photos[public]&#96; | Maintain minimum 3 CONTEXT_LINKS (TESTIMONY/EXPERT/DOCUMENT) |\n| **DOCUMENT** | &#96;embedding(1536d)&#96;, &#96;url&#96;, &#96;file[]&#96; | Generate vector embeddings for all text content |\n| **ARTIFACT** | &#96;name[unique]&#96;, &#96;origin&#96;, &#96;images[public]&#96; | Verify against multiple source testimonies |\n| **SIGHTING** | &#96;shape&#96;, &#96;duration_seconds&#96;, &#96;media_link&#96; | Enforce location[lat/long] validation |\n\n### 2. Relationship Mapping Matrix\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[PERSON] --\u003e|PERSON_ORGANIZATION| B[ORGANIZATION]\n    C[EVENT] --\u003e|EVENT_EXPERT| A\n    D[TOPIC] --\u003e|TOPIC_EXPERT| A\n    C --\u003e|EVENT_TOPIC_EXPERT| D\n    D --\u003e|TOPIC_TESTIMONY| E[TESTIMONY]\n    F[SIGHTING] --\u003e|occurs_at| G[LOCATION]\n    H[ARTIFACT] --\u003e|found_at| G\n    I[DOCUMENT] --\u003e|references| C\n    I --\u003e|contains| E\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3.         "contents": "# Entity Extraction Workflow Preservation Plan\n\n**Date:** July 9, 2025 at 07:25 PST  \n**Purpose:** Preserve existing entity extraction workflow while integrating Triple RAG capabilities  \n**Status:** Implementation Plan - Ready for Execution\n\n## Executive Summary\n\nThe existing entity extraction workflow is a sophisticated system that processes YouTube transcripts, extracts structured entities using AI, and searches for matches in a comprehensive Xata database. This plan preserves all existing functionality while enhancing the system with Triple RAG search capabilities (Upstash + LocalRAG + CocoIndex) for improved entity matching and discovery.\n\n## Current System Architecture Analysis\n\n### Core Components (✅ PRESERVE UNCHANGED)\n\n#### 1. **Entity Extraction Agent** (&#96;agents/entity_extraction_agent.py&#96;)\n- **AI-Powered Extraction**: Uses OpenAI/Anthropic for structured entity extraction\n- **Comprehensive Schema**: Supports 9 entity types + relationships\n- **Entity Types**: Topics, Personnel, Events, Organizations, Locations, Technologies, Dates, Artifacts, Sightings\n- **Confidence Scoring**: 0-1 confidence scores for each extracted entity\n- **Metadata Extraction**: Rich metadata for each entity type\n- **Relationship Detection**: Identifies connections between entities\n\n#### 2. **Interactive Entity Processor** (&#96;lib/interactive_entity_processor.py&#96;)\n- **User Interface**: Rich console interface with progress indicators\n- **Batch Processing**: Processes multiple entity types efficiently\n- **Result Storage**: Saves results to JSON files\n- **Interactive/Non-interactive Modes**: Supports both modes\n\n#### 3. **Xata Search Integration** (&#96;lib/xata_search.py&#96;)\n- **Fuzzy Search**: Configurable search with fuzziness\n- **Multi-field Search**: Searches across relevant table columns\n- **Database Tables**: Maps to personnel, organizations, topics, events, locations\n- **Confidence Filtering**: Filters results by confidence threshold\n\n### Data Schema (✅ PRESERVE COMPLETELY)\n\n",

        "originalContents": "# Entity Extraction Workflow Preservation Plan\n\n**Date:** July 9, 2025 at 07:25 PST  \n**Purpose:** Preserve existing entity extraction workflow while integrating Triple RAG capabilities  \n**Status:** Implementation Plan - Ready for Execution\n\n## Executive Summary\n\nThe existing entity extraction workflow is a sophisticated system that processes YouTube transcripts, extracts structured entities using AI, and searches for matches in a comprehensive Xata database. This plan preserves all existing functionality while enhancing the system with Triple RAG search capabilities (Upstash + LocalRAG + CocoIndex) for improved entity matching and discovery.\n\n## Current System Architecture Analysis\n\n### Core Components (✅ PRESERVE UNCHANGED)\n\n#### 1. **Entity Extraction Agent** (&#96;agents/entity_extraction_agent.py&#96;)\n- **AI-Powered Extraction**: Uses OpenAI/Anthropic for structured entity extraction\n- **Comprehensive Schema**: Supports 9 entity types + relationships\n- **Entity Types**: Topics, Personnel, Events, Organizations, Locations, Technologies, Dates, Artifacts, Sightings\n- **Confidence Scoring**: 0-1 confidence scores for each extracted entity\n- **Metadata Extraction**: Rich metadata for each entity type\n- **Relationship Detection**: Identifies connections between entities\n\n#### 2. **Interactive Entity Processor** (&#96;lib/interactive_entity_processor.py&#96;)\n- **User Interface**: Rich console interface with progress indicators\n- **Batch Processing**: Processes multiple entity types efficiently\n- **Result Storage**: Saves results to JSON files\n- **Interactive/Non-interactive Modes**: Supports both modes\n\n#### 3. **Xata Search Integration** (&#96;lib/xata_search.py&#96;)\n- **Fuzzy Search**: Configurable search with fuzziness\n- **Multi-field Search**: Searches across relevant table columns\n- **Database Tables**: Maps to personnel, organizations, topics, events, locations\n- **Confidence Filtering**: Filters results by confidence threshold\n\n### Data Schema (✅ PRESERVE COMPLETELY)\n\n",

        "contents": "\"\"\"\nNamed Entity Recognition and Xata Table Conversion Prompt\n\nThis module contains the prompt used for named entity recognition in UAP/UFO documents\nand conversion to Xata table structures.\n\"\"\"\n\nner_prompt = \"\"\"\nYou are a specialized entity extraction system for UFO/UAP research documents.\nExtract structured entities from the provided content following these guidelines:\n\n# Entity Categories \u0026 Schema\n\n## 1. TOPICS\n- Required fields: &#96;name&#96;, &#96;summary&#96;\n- Extract all significant UFO/UAP topics mentioned\n- Include technical capabilities, phenomena types, and classifications\n- Rate each topic's significance from 1-100\n\n## 2. PERSONNEL\n- Required fields: &#96;name&#96;, &#96;role&#96;, &#96;rank&#96;, &#96;credibility&#96;, &#96;authority&#96;\n- Extract all named individuals relevant to UFO/UAP research\n- Identify their roles (Witness, Researcher, Official, etc.)\n- Rate their rank/importance (1-100)\n- Rate their credibility (1-100)\n- Rate their scientific/official authority (1-100)\n\n## 3. EVENTS\n- Required fields: &#96;name&#96;, &#96;date&#96;, &#96;location&#96;, &#96;description&#96;\n- Extract all UFO/UAP incidents or events\n- Include as precise details as available (date/location)\n- If exact date unavailable, use approximate (e.g., \"mid-1990s\")\n- Rate significance from 1-100\n\n## 4. ORGANIZATIONS\n- Required fields: &#96;name&#96;, &#96;type&#96;, &#96;description&#96;\n- Extract all organizations involved with UFO/UAP research\n- Specify type (Government, Military, Research, etc.)\n- Include relationship to the topic\n- Rate significance from 1-100\n\n# Output Format\n\nReturn the extracted entities as a JSON object with these keys:\n- &#96;topics&#96;: Array of topic objects\n- &#96;personnel&#96;: Array of personnel objects\n- &#96;events&#96;: Array of event objects\n- &#96;organizations&#96;: Array of organization objects\n\nExample format:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"topics\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"Tic-Tac UAP\",\n      \"summary\": \"White oblong craft observed by Navy pilots in 2004\",\n      \"significance\": 95\n    }\n  ],\n  \"personnel\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"Commander David Fravor\",\n      \"role\": \"Navy Pilot Witness\",\n      \"rank\": 85,\n      \"credibility\": 90,\n      \"authority\": 88\n    }\n  ],\n  \"events\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"USS Nimitz Encounter\",\n      \"date\": \"November 14, 2004\",\n      \"location\": \"Pacific Ocean, off San Diego\",\n      \"description\": \"Navy pilots encountered tic-tac shaped UAP showing advanced capabilities\",\n      \"significance\": 98\n    }\n  ],\n  \"organizations\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"AATIP\",\n      \"type\": \"Government Program\",\n      \"description\": \"Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, Pentagon UAP study\",\n      \"significance\": 95\n    }\n  ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n# Guidelines\n\n- Extract entities ONLY if they appear in the text\n- Do not invent or assume entities not explicitly mentioned\n- Use the exact names/terms as they appear in the text\n- If exact values for required fields aren't available, use \"Unknown\"\n- For numeric ratings, use your judgment based on context\n- Focus on extracting ALL relevant entities, even briefly mentioned ones\n- Maintain objectivity and avoid speculation\n",

Extract structured data from any input source (websites, documents, PDFs) using strict schema compliance for vector embeddings and SQL processing.**\n\n## Entity Extraction Protocol\n\n### 1. Core Entity Recognition\n\n| Entity Type | Priority Fields | Extraction Rules |\n|-------------|-----------------|------------------|\n| **PERSON** | &#96;role&#96;, &#96;credibility(1-10)&#96;, &#96;authority(1-10)&#96;, &#96;bio&#96; | Validate against ORGANIZATION memberships and EVENT participation |\n| **EVENT** | &#96;title[unique]&#96;, &#96;datetime&#96;, &#96;location(coordinates)&#96;, &#96;metadata&#96; | Link to minimum 2 RELATED_ENTITIES (PERSON/ORGANIZATION/TOPIC) |\n| **ORGANIZATION** | &#96;title[unique]&#96;, &#96;specialization&#96;, &#96;image[public]&#96; | Map hierarchy through PERSON_ORGANIZATION relations |\n| **LOCATION** | &#96;coordinates&#96;, &#96;google_maps_id&#96;, &#96;city/state&#96; | Geocode all spatial references |\n| **TESTIMONY** | &#96;claim&#96;, &#96;source&#96;, &#96;documentation[]&#96; | Cross-link to TOPIC_TESTIMONY and EVENT entities |\n| **TOPIC** | &#96;title[unique]&#96;, &#96;summary&#96;, &#96;photos[public]&#96; | Maintain minimum 3 CONTEXT_LINKS (TESTIMONY/EXPERT/DOCUMENT) |\n| **DOCUMENT** | &#96;embedding(1536d)&#96;, &#96;url&#96;, &#96;file[]&#96; | Generate vector embeddings for all text content |\n| **ARTIFACT** | &#96;name[unique]&#96;, &#96;origin&#96;, &#96;images[public]&#96; | Verify against multiple source testimonies |\n| **SIGHTING** | &#96;shape&#96;, &#96;duration_seconds&#96;, &#96;media_link&#96; | Enforce location[lat/long] validation |\n\n### 2. Relationship Mapping Matrix\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[PERSON] --\u003e|PERSON_ORGANIZATION| B[ORGANIZATION]\n    C[EVENT] --\u003e|EVENT_EXPERT| A\n    D[TOPIC] --\u003e|TOPIC_EXPERT| A\n    C --\u003e|EVENT_TOPIC_EXPERT| D\n    D --\u003e|TOPIC_TESTIMONY| E[TESTIMONY]\n    F[SIGHTING] --\u003e|occurs_at| G[LOCATION]\n    H[ARTIFACT] --\u003e|found_at| G\n    I[DOCUMENT] --\u003e|references| C\n    I --\u003e|contains| E\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. Extraction Confidence Framework\n\n",

Extract name, type, jurisdiction, security_level\n       - Include parent/subsidiary relationships\n       - Document key personnel associations\n       - Organization types: AGENCY, RESEARCH_GROUP, MILITARY, CIVILIAN_ORG\n\n    4. **LOCATION entities** (facilities, sighting locations, coordinates):\n       - Extract coordinates, address, geohash\n       - Include activity metrics and security classification\n       - Document geographic patterns\n\n    5. **ARTIFACT entities** (physical evidence, debris, media):\n       - Extract name, type, discovery details, chain of custody\n       - Include physical properties and analysis status\n       - Document security classification\n\n    6. **SIGHTING entities** (UAP observations):\n       - Extract date, location, description, shape, duration\n       - Include witness information and media links\n       - Document environmental conditions\n\n    7. **TESTIMONY entities** (witness accounts, statements):\n       - Extract claims, sources, context, documentation\n       - Link to events, witnesses, organizations\n       - Include verification status\n\n    8. **TOPIC entities** (subjects, theories, concepts):\n       - Extract name, title, summary\n       - Include related documentation and media\n\n    9. **RELATIONSHIPS**:\n       - Personnel → Organization (works_for, member_of)\n       - Event → Location (occurred_at)\n       - Event → Person (witnessed_by, investigated_by)\n       - Testimony → Event (describes, relates_to)\n       - Artifact → Location (discovered_at)\n       - Organization → Location (stationed_at)\n       - His work led to an information revolution and the unprecedented mass-spread / \n    of literature throughout Europe. Moreover, they can produce a &#96;JSON&#96; response that conforms to the &#96;function&#96; signature. Here's the sequence we follow:\n\n1. Define our &#96;function&#96; and its associated &#96;JSON&#96; Schema.\n2. Invoke the model using the &#96;messages&#96;, &#96;tools&#96; and &#96;tool_choice&#96; parameters.\n3. Convert the output into a &#96;JSON&#96; object, and then call the &#96;function&#96; with the &#96;arguments&#96; provided by the model.\n\nIn practice, one might want to re-invoke the model again by appending the &#96;function&#96; response as a new message, and let the model summarize the results back to the user. Nevertheless, for our purposes, this step is not needed.\n\n_Note that in a real-case scenario it is strongly recommended to build in user confirmation flows before taking actions._\n\n#### 4.1 Define our Function and JSON schema\n\nSince we want the model to output a dictionary of labels and recognized entities:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{   \n    \"gpe\": [\"Germany\", \"Europe\"],   \n    \"date\": [\"1440\"],   \n    \"person\": [\"Johannes Gutenberg\"],   \n    \"product\": [\"movable-type printing press\"],   \n    \"event\": [\"Renaissance\"],   \n    \"quantity\": [\"3,600 pages\"],   \n    \"time\": [\"workday\"]   \n}   \n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nwe need to define the corresponding &#96;JSON&#96; schema to be passed to the &#96;tools&#96; parameter:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ndef generate_functions(labels: dict) -\u003e list:\n    return [\n        {   \n            \"type\": \"function\",\n            \"function\": {\n                \"name\": \"enrich_entities\",\n                \"description\": \"Enrich Text with Knowledge Base Links\",\n                \"parameters\": {\n                    \"type\": \"object\",\n                        \"properties\": {\n                            \"r'^(?:' + '|'.join({labels}) + ')$'\": \n                            {\n                                \"type\": \"array\",\n                                \"items\": {\n                                    \"type\": \"string\"\n                                }\n                            }\n                        },\n                        \"additionalProperties\": False\n                },\n            }\n        }\n    ]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 4.2 Chat Completion\n\nNow, we invoke the model. It's important to note that we direct the API to use a specific function by setting the &#96;tool_choice&#96; parameter to &#96;{\"type\": \"function\", \"function\" : {\"name\": \"enrich_entities\"}}&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n@retry(wait=wait_random_exponential(min=1, max=10), stop=stop_after_attempt(5))\ndef run_openai_task(labels, text):\n    messages = [\n          {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": system_message(labels=labels)},\n          {\"role\": \"assistant\", \"content\": assisstant_message()},\n          {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": user_message(text=text)}\n      ]\n\n    # TODO: functions and function_call are deprecated, need to be updated\n    # See: https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/create#chat-create-tools\n    response = openai.chat.completions.create(\n        model=\"gpt-3.5-turbo-0613\",\n        messages=messages,\n        tools=generate_functions(labels),\n        tool_choice={\"type\": \"function\", \"function\" : {\"name\": \"enrich_entities\"}}, \n        temperature=0,\n        frequency_penalty=0,\n        presence_penalty=0,\n    )\n\n    response_message = response.choices[0].message\n    \n    available_functions = {\"enrich_entities\": enrich_entities}  \n    function_name = response_message.tool_calls[0].function.name\n    \n    function_to_call = available_functions[function_name]\n    logging.info(f\"function_to_call: {function_to_call}\")\n\n    function_args = json.loads(response_message.tool_calls[0].function.arguments)\n    logging.info(f\"function_args: {function_args}\")\n\n    function_response = function_to_call(text, function_args)\n\n    return {\"model_response\": response, \n            \"function_response\": function_response}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 5\\. Let's Enrich a Text with Wikipedia links\n\n#### 5.1 Run OpenAI Task\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ntext = \"\"\"The Beatles were an English rock band formed in Liverpool in 1960, comprising John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr.\"\"\"\nresult = run_openai_task(labels, text)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n 2023-10-20 18:05:51,729 - INFO - function_to_call: \u003cfunction enrich_entities at 0x0000021D30C462A0\u003e\n 2023-10-20 18:05:51,730 - INFO - function_args: {'person': ['John Lennon', 'Paul McCartney', 'George Harrison', 'Ringo Starr'], 'org': ['The Beatles'], 'gpe': ['Liverpool'], 'date': ['1960']}\n 2023-10-20 18:06:09,858 - INFO - entity_link_dict: {'John Lennon': 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon', 'Paul McCartney': 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney', 'George Harrison': 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Harrison', 'Ringo Starr': 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ringo_Starr', 'The Beatles': 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles', 'Liverpool': 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool'}\n\n#### 5.2 Function Response\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ndisplay(Markdown(f\"\"\"**Text:** {text}   \n                     **Enriched_Text:** {result['function_response']}\"\"\"))\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\u003cIPython.core.display.Markdown object\u003e\n\n#### 5.3 Token Usage\n\nTo estimate the inference costs, we can parse the response's \"usage\" field. Detailed token costs per model are available in the OpenAI Pricing Guide:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n# estimate inference cost assuming gpt-3.5-turbo (4K context)\ni_tokens  = result[\"model_response\"].usage.prompt_tokens \no_tokens = result[\"model_response\"].usage.completion_tokens \n\ni_cost = (i_tokens / 1000) * 0.0015\no_cost = (o_tokens / 1000) * 0.002\n\nprint(f\"\"\"Token Usage\n    Prompt: {i_tokens} tokens\n    Completion: {o_tokens} tokens\n    Cost estimation: ${round(i_cost + o_cost, 5)}\"\"\")\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nToken Usage\n    Prompt: 331 tokens\n    Completion: 47 tokens\n    Cost estimation: $0.00059",
      "title": "Named Entity Recognition to Enrich Text | OpenAI Cookbook",
      "url": "https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/named_entity_recognition_to_enrich_text"
    },

Report Abuse \n\nCover image for Advanced Entity Extraction with Azure OpenAI: Harnessing Structured Outputs \n\nUmesh Tharuka Malaviarachchi \n\nUmesh Tharuka Malaviarachchi \n\n Posted on Dec 5, 2024 \n\n#  Advanced Entity Extraction with Azure OpenAI: Harnessing Structured Outputs\n\n#webdev #programming #devops #opensource \n\nEntity extraction is a powerful tool in natural language processing (NLP), enabling applications to identify and categorize data points such as names, dates, or locations from text. Azure OpenAI Service now supports structured outputs, elevating the efficiency of entity extraction tasks by returning results in user-defined formats such as JSON, XML, or tabular data. This article explores how to implement and optimize entity extraction using Azure OpenAI’s structured outputs. \n\n---\n\n#### **Why Use Structured Outputs for Entity Extraction?** \n\nTraditional entity extraction requires significant post-processing to organize raw outputs into usable formats. Azure OpenAI simplifies this by allowing developers to define the desired output structure within prompts. Benefits include: \n\n1. **Efficiency:** Eliminates additional processing steps, reducing development time.\n2. **Accuracy:** Ensures extracted entities conform to predefined formats, minimizing errors.\n3. **Integration-Ready:** Structured outputs can be directly fed into downstream systems such as databases, APIs, or dashboards.\n\n---\n\n#### **Setting Up Azure OpenAI for Entity Extraction** \n\n1. **Provision Azure OpenAI Resources:**  \n   * Navigate to the Azure portal and create an Azure OpenAI resource.  \n   * Select the desired model, such as GPT-4, for advanced NLP capabilities.\n2. **Define Prompt Structure:**  \n    \nUse prompt engineering to guide the model in returning structured outputs. For example:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n   Extract entities from the following text and return in JSON format:  \n   Input: \"John Doe was born on July 4, 1980, in New York City and works at Contoso Corporation.\"  \n   Output Format: {\"Name\": \"\", \"Date of Birth\": \"\", \"Location\": \"\", \"Company\": \"\"}  \n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nEnter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode \n\n1. **Invoke the API:**Use Azure OpenAI REST API or SDKs (e.g., Python or .NET) to send requests. Specify the structured format in the payload to ensure consistent results.\n\n---\n\n#### **Advanced Techniques** \n\n1. **Handling Ambiguities in Text:**Train the model with example-rich prompts to handle contextually ambiguous scenarios. For instance:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n   Extract entities while distinguishing between personal names and brand names.  \n   Input: \"Apple released its new iPhone, and Steve Jobs' legacy continues.\"  \n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nEnter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode \n\n1. **Custom Named Entity Recognition (NER):**  \n    \nUse Azure OpenAI alongside Azure Cognitive Services to build domain-specific NER models. For example, extract technical terms from research papers or compliance-related entities from legal documents.\n2. **Validation and Post-Processing:**  \n    \nImplement additional validation checks in your application to handle edge cases where the model's output might deviate from the expected structure.\n3. **Data Integration Pipelines:**  \n    \nCombine Azure OpenAI with Azure Logic Apps or Azure Data Factory to automate the flow of extracted entities into business workflows or reporting systems.\n\n---\n\n#### **Applications of Structured Entity Extraction** \n\n1. **Customer Relationship Management (CRM):**  \n    \nAutomatically extract customer information from emails, chats, or forms and populate CRM systems.\n2. **Compliance and Legal:**  \n    \nIdentify and organize regulatory terms, clauses, or personal identifiable information (PII) from contracts and documents.\n3. **Healthcare:**  \n    \nExtract patient data, medical terms, or diagnoses from clinical notes for electronic health records (EHRs).\n4. **Market Research:**  \n    \nAnalyze survey responses or social media posts by extracting key sentiments, names, or trends.\n\n---\n\n#### **Best Practices** \n\n1. **Iterative Prompt Design:**  \n    \nContinuously refine prompts based on model outputs to improve accuracy and relevance.\n2. **Leverage Multiple Azure Services:**  \n    \nPair Azure OpenAI with Cognitive Search for entity search or Synapse Analytics for large-scale data analysis.\n3. **Monitoring and Feedback:**  \n    \nMonitor the model’s outputs over time and incorporate user feedback to retrain or adjust prompts for better results.\n\n---\n\n#### **Conclusion** \n\nAzure OpenAI’s structured outputs for entity extraction revolutionize how businesses process unstructured text data. By leveraging this capability, developers can build robust, scalable applications that extract actionable insights with minimal effort. Whether you’re optimizing customer experiences, ensuring compliance, or advancing data-driven research, Azure OpenAI provides the tools to redefine efficiency in NLP tasks. \n\nTo dive deeper into implementation details, visit the official Microsoft Tech Community article. \n\n##  Top comments (0) \n\nSubscribe \n\npic \n\nPersonal Trusted User \n\n Create template \n\nTemplates let you quickly answer FAQs or store snippets for re-use.\n\nSubmit Preview Dismiss \n\nCode of Conduct • Report abuse \n\n Are you sure you want to hide this comment?       "chunk": "Towards Data Science\n\nPublish AI, ML \u0026 data-science insights to a global community of data professionals.\n\nSign in\n\nSign out\n\nSubmit an Article\n\n* Latest\n* Editor’s Picks\n* Deep Dives\n* Newsletter\n\n---\n\n* Write For TDS\n\nTowards Data Science\n\nToggle Mobile Navigation \n\n* LinkedIn\n* X\n\nToggle Search \n\nSearch\n\n# Advanced NER With GPT-3 and GPT-J\n\n GPT-3 and GPT-J are very good at performing advanced entity extraction without having to be trained for that. Let's see how to extract… \n\nMaxime Cupani\n\nApr 28, 2022\n\n 8 min read\n\n Share \n\n# Advanced NER With GPT-4, LLaMA, and Mixtral\n\nGenerative deep learning models based on Transformers appeared a couple of years ago. GPT-4, LLaMA, and Mixtral 8x7B are the most advanced text generation models today and they are so powerful that they pretty much revolutionized many legacy NLP use cases. Entity extraction (NER) is one of them.\n\nIn this article we will see how to use GPT models to perform advanced entity extraction without annotating any data. Annotating and training one’s own NER model has always been a challenge, but fortunately it’s not necessary anymore!\n\nAs GPT-4 can be quite expensive, all our examples will be based on LLaMA 2 through the NLP Cloud API for quick prototyping.\n\nFrench Alps (image by the author)\n\nFrench Alps (image by the author)\n\n### Doing NER The Old Way\n\nEntity extraction is one of the oldest NLP use cases, and maybe one of the most common NLP use cases deployed in production today. Traditionally, frameworks like spaCy and NLTK used to be the best choices.\n\nSpaCy is well suited for production because it is both easy to use and extremely fast when running in production. SpaCy offers many pre-trained models that one can easily download and start using right away in production. Several native entities are supported out of the box by the spaCy models like addresses, dates, currencies…\n\nNLTK is not suited for production but it is a great tool for research projects and ramp up on NLP. NLTK proposes some pre-trained models too, but with less native entities than spaCy.\n\nThe major problem with these pre-trained models is that they only support the native entities they were trained for… and these entities are rarely useful in real life projects. Most companies want to use NER to extract custom entities like job titles, product names, movie titles, restaurants, etc. The only solution was to create a huge dataset for these new entities through a long and tedious annotation process, and then train a new model. Everytime one wanted to support a new entity, the only solution was to annotate and train again. Great annotation tools like Prodigy really help, but it still requires a lot of work involving one or several human resources on a potentially long period.\n\nHopefully, generative large language models now solve this problem.\n\n### What Are GPT-4, LLaMA, and Mixtral?\n\nIn May 2020, OpenAI released a huge generative model: GPT-3\\. In March 2023, OpenAI released GPT-4.\n\nGPT-4 is a large language model based on Transformers that revolutionized the NLP field. The GPT-3 model was trained on 175B parameters, and OpenAI never disclosed the number of parameters behind GPT-4\\. This model is so complex that it can understand many human queries without having to be explicitly trained for that. It can pretty much do everything that traditional NLP models did: NER, summarization, translation, classification… and much more.\n\nGPT-4 has a couple of weaknesses though:\n\n* It is very expensive and can only be used through the OpenAI API\n* It is quite slow (compared to frameworks like spaCy)\n* It is not necessarily easy to use\n\nGood news is that open-source alternatives were released in 2023 too: LLaMA 2 by Meta, and Mixtral 8x7B by Mistral AI. These NLP models can be deployed by anyone on any server, but in practice it takes some MLOps knowledge and it can be quite costly, which is why we are going to use the NLP Cloud API that is both affordable and easy to use.\n\n### Set Up NLP Cloud\n\nFirst, register on NLP Cloud.\n\nThen switch to the pay-as-you-go plan as this plan allows you to use LLaMA 2 and Mixtral as much as you want and gives you a $15 free credit, which will be more than enough to test the code in this article.\n\nRetrieve your API token.\n\nLast of all, download their Python Client as we will use it in the following examples:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\npip install nlpcloud\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Prompt Engineering\n\nLet’s say we want to extract job titles from a piece of text.\n\nLet’s make a first naive request to Mixtral:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport nlpcloud\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient = nlpcloud.Client(\"mixtral-8x7b\", \"\u003cyour_token\u003e\", gpu=True)\ngeneration = client.generation(\"\"\"Extract job titles from the following sentence: Maxime is a data scientist at Auto Dataset, and he's been working there for 1 year.\"\"\")\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nprint(generation[\"generated_text\"])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nOutput:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nExtract job titles from the following sentence: Maxime is a data scientist at Auto Dataset, and he's been working there for 1 year.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1. Maxime works in the data science team at Auto Dataset.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAs you can see, we miserably failed! The reason is that generative models like LLaMA and Mixtral need a couple of examples in the prompt in order to understand what you want (also known as \"few-shot learning\"). The prompt is basically a piece of text that you will add before your actual request.\n\nLet’s try again with 3 examples in the prompt:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport nlpcloud\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient = nlpcloud.Client(\"mixtral-8x7b\", \"\u003cyour_token\u003e\", gpu=True)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ngeneration = client.generation(\"\"\"[Text]: Helena Smith founded Core.ai 2 years ago. She is now the CEO and CTO of the company and is building a team of highly skilled developers in machine learning and natural language processing.\n        [Position]: CEO and CTO\n        ###\n        [Text]: Tech Robotics is a robot automation company specialized in AI driven robotization. Its Chief Technology Officer, Max Smith, says a new wave of improvements should be expected for next year.\n        [Position]: Chief Technology Officer\n        ###\n        [Text]: François is a Go developer. He mostly works as a freelancer but is open to any kind of job offering!\n        [Position]: Go developer\n        ###\n        [Text]: Maxime is a data scientist at Auto Dataset, and he's been working there for 1 year.\n        [Position]:\"\"\",\n    max_length=500,\n    end_sequence=\"n###\",\n    remove_end_sequence=True,\n    remove_input=True)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nprint(generation[\"generated_text\"])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nOutput:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nData scientist\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIt worked! What happened here?\n\nFirst, we gave 3 questions and 3 responses to the model in the prompt, before passing our actual sentence. 3 examples are usually enough to teach these models what you want to achieve.\n\nWe also used a couple of parameters:\n\n* &#96;max_length&#96; tells the API to generate 500 tokens maximum\n* &#96;end_sequence=\"n###\"&#96; tells the model to stop generating text once it reaches &#96;n###&#96;. It makes the text generation much faster since we don’t have to wait until the 500 tokens are generated (and it is also cheaper). We know that the model will add &#96;n###&#96;token after the result because we added it after each result in the prompt, and Mixtral is very good at learning formatting.\n* &#96;remove_end_sequence&#96; simply removes &#96;n###&#96;at the end of the response.\n* &#96;remove_input&#96; removes the input from the response\n\nDoing the same thing with spaCy would have taken a dedicated dataset + training with tons of examples… in other words, we just saved weeks, or even months of human work!\n\n### Improvements\n\nWe just made a first proof of concept for entity extraction with Mixtral, but we can of course improve it.\n\nThe first thing we should do is lower the Top P value. Top P and Temperature are 2 common parameters of generative models. High values tends to produce more original results, which is not what we want here as we want the model to consistently extract the same entity in a deterministic way without inventing anything. The best way to do it is to lower Top P to 0.1.\n\nThe second thing we should care about is the ability to handle empty responses. It can indeed happen that your piece of text does not contain any job title, and in that case you want the model to return something like \"none\" (for example). So you need to explicitly tell the model about it.\n\nLet’s implement these 2 improvements:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport nlpcloud\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient = nlpcloud.Client(\"mixtral-8x7b\", \"\u003cyour_token\u003e\", gpu=True)\ngeneration = client.generation(\"\"\"[Text]: Helena Smith founded Core.ai 2 years ago. She is now the CEO and CTO of the company and is building a team of highly skilled developers in machine learning and natural language processing.\n        [Position]: CEO and CTO\n        ###\n        [Text]: Tech Robotics is a robot automation company specialized in AI driven robotization. Its Chief Technology Officer, Max Smith, says a new wave of improvements should be expected for next year.\n        [Position]: Chief Technology Officer\n        ###\n        [Text]: François is a Go developer. He mostly works as a freelancer but is open to any kind of job offering!\n        [Position]: Go developer\n        ###\n        [Text]: The second thing we should care about is the ability to handle empty responses.\n        [Position]: none\n        ###\n        [Text]: Maxime is a data scientist at Auto Dataset, and he's been working there for 1 year.\n        [Position]:\"\"\",\n    max_length=500,\n    top_p=0.1,    \n    end_sequence=\"n###\",\n    remove_end_sequence=True,\n    remove_input=True)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nprint(generation[\"generated_text\"])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can improve your prompt even more by handling mutliple results for example (i.e. extract several job titles from the same piece of text).\n\n### Production Deployment\n\nThe main weakness of these generative models is that they are costly to efficiently run in production and they require some advanced DevOps knowledge.\n\nFor example you should forget about running Mixtral and LLaMA on your own local machine or even on a CPU server. If you want it to extract your entity in a decent time (below 1 second), you will need to use a modern GPUs like the NVIDIA A40, the NVIDIA A100, or the NVIDIA H100.\n\n---\n\n### Conclusion\n\nEntity extraction with GPT-4, LLaMA, and Mixtral gives impressive results as soon as you understand how to deal with prompting.\n\nAs no more annotation and training is required, I think it will considerably change the way NER projects are organized.\n\nThere are still some infrastructure challenges though, but I think they are negligible compared to the human costs of data labeling.\n\nI hope found this article useful and it will give you new ideas for your next NER project!\n\n---\n\nWritten By\n\nMaxime Cupani\n\nSee all from Maxime Cupani\n\nGpt 4, Llama 2, Mixtral 8x7b, Ner, Spacy\n\nShare This Article\n\n* Share on Facebook\n* Share on LinkedIn\n* Share on X\n\nTowards Data Science is a community publication.
